reasoning: The claim is scientifically accurate and widely verified by space agencies such as NASA. Precise measurements obtained via the Lunar Laser Ranging Experiment—which bounces lasers off retroreflectors placed on the lunar surface during the Apollo missions—confirm that the Moon is moving away from Earth at a rate of approximately 3.8 centimeters (about 1.5 inches) per year. This phenomenon, known as lunar recession, is caused by tidal friction. The gravitational pull of the Moon creates tidal bulges on Earth, and because Earth rotates faster than the Moon orbits it, these bulges pull the Moon forward, transferring rotational kinetic energy into orbital energy and gradually pushing the Moon into a higher, wider orbit. At this rate, in approximately 500 million to 1 billion years, the Moon will be too far from Earth to completely cover the Sun, meaning total solar eclipses will no longer occur.
